AUTHORED FIGURE BRIEF:
This figure presents six diagrams of the three cubic unit cell types — simple cubic, body-centered cubic (BCC), and face-centered cubic (FCC) — arranged in two rows of three: a top row titled "Lattice point locations" showing schematic dot-and-line cube diagrams, and a bottom row titled "Cubic unit cells" showing space-filling sphere models, with each column sharing a label (Simple cubic, Body-centered cubic, Face-centered cubic) at the bottom. In the top-row schematic diagrams, the simple cubic cell has black dots only at the eight corners; the BCC cell adds one red dot at the body center; and the FCC cell adds red dots at the center of each face while retaining black dots at all corners. In the bottom-row space-filling models, the simple cubic unit cell shows gray corner spheres touching along cube edges with no central atom; the BCC model highlights the single body-center atom in orange, showing it in contact with all eight gray corner atoms; and the FCC model shows multiple orange face-centered atoms contacting both the gray corner atoms and neighboring face atoms along face diagonals. By pairing each abstract lattice-point diagram directly above its corresponding space-filling model, the figure makes explicit how lattice geometry translates into actual atomic packing and allows the number of atoms per unit cell to be counted for each type. This figure introduces the three cubic unit cells as the fundamental repeating units of metallic crystal lattices and establishes the atom-counting framework needed to calculate density and relate crystal structure to bulk properties.

REQUESTED INTERACTIONS:
- Toggle between simple cubic, body-centered cubic, and face-centered cubic: update both the lattice point diagram (top row) and the space-filling sphere model (bottom row) simultaneously
- Click any atom in the space-filling model: highlight its fractional contribution (1/8 for corner, 1/2 for face, 1 for body center) and display the total atoms per unit cell

SOURCE FILE: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, chapter 10

PROJECTION (inspect the source image, choose exactly one, and call setCameraView accordingly):
  perspective:
    Use the scaffold's true perspective projection after building all geometry. Use this only when the source has real vanishing-point convergence or distance-based size shrinkage; then depth should visibly affect apparent size.

  axonometric:
    Use ordinary orthographic projection: setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles, heightFraction }). If the source is a flat 2D plot or diagram, pass axisScreenAngles: null for a front-on view. Otherwise do not try to measure per-figure angles from the image — use a standard isometric pose: axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }. The source image is a PROJECTION of a 3D object: rebuild the true object — a rectangle stays a rectangle in world space — and let the camera do the projecting. Never bake the drawn parallelogram into the geometry, and never shear geometry. Omit zoom and call setCameraView after all geometry is added — the scaffold auto-fits from the projected bounding box.

  oblique:
    Call setCameraView({ projection: 'oblique', obliqueAngleDeg: 45, depthScale: 0.5, heightFraction }) after all geometry is added — a standard cabinet-oblique pose; do not try to measure per-figure oblique angles from the image. The scaffold implements oblique as a shear of the eye-space projection matrix, so the front face stays undistorted, depth edges leave at obliqueAngleDeg, and labels track the shear automatically. Build the TRUE 3D object — the shear is the camera's job. Do NOT shear geometry, do NOT wrap the figure in a sheared parent Object3D, and do NOT disable automatic matrix updates. The scaffold also provides the reveal interaction: dragging eases the shear out to expose the real 3D shape and a toggle button returns to the printed view — do not implement either yourself.
AXIS ASSIGNMENT: the pose is pinned, so in BoxGeometry(w, h, d) the w axis is screen-right, h is screen-up, and d is the receding diagonal. Before writing each BoxGeometry, look at the source image and decide which of the object's dimensions actually recedes there — do not assume it is the one the domain calls "depth". In feature-map / layer-stack diagrams the channel count is usually the w (horizontal) extent along the flow direction and a spatial dimension is d. Sanity-check the silhouette against the source: a block that should read as a long bar pointing at its neighbours must be long in w, not in d, or it will render as a sliver shooting into the page. If your chosen axis assignment contradicts the source image's silhouette, follow the image.

Build the figure directly from the brief above and the source image. There is no interaction plan: decide the elements, geometry, labels, and controls yourself.

Cubic unit cell type
Selected: Simple cubic
Total atoms per unit cell: 1
Click a sphere in the lower models to see how much of that atom belongs to one unit cell.
// @FIGURE_CODE_BEGIN // top schematic cube → transparent pale-green BoxGeometry + black EdgesGeometry // top corner lattice points → small black SphereGeometry at eight cube corners // top BCC body point → small red SphereGeometry at cube center // top FCC face points → small red SphereGeometry at six face centers // lower unit-cell cage → transparent pale-green BoxGeometry + black EdgesGeometry // lower corner atoms → gray shaded SphereGeometry centered on cube corners // lower body-centered atom → orange shaded SphereGeometry at cube center // lower face-centered atoms → orange shaded SphereGeometry at six face centers // selection indicators → yellow LineLoop rectangles around chosen column diagrams scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.72)); const keyLight = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.92); keyLight.position.set(3, 5, 4); scene.add(keyLight); const fillLight = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.35); fillLight.position.set(-4, 2, -3); scene.add(fillLight); const TYPES = { sc: { name: 'Simple cubic', short: 'SC', total: 1 }, bcc: { name: 'Body-centered cubic', short: 'BCC', total: 2 }, fcc: { name: 'Face-centered cubic', short: 'FCC', total: 4 } }; const cols = { sc: -1.75, bcc: 0, fcc: 1.75 }; const typeOrder = ['sc', 'bcc', 'fcc']; const groupsByType = {}; const atoms = []; const selectedFrames = []; function matLine(color = 0x000000, opacity = 1) { return new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color, transparent: opacity < 1, opacity }); } function matCube(opacity = 0.34) { return new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xcfe6b5, transparent: true, opacity, depthWrite: false, side: THREE.DoubleSide }); } function matSphere(color, opacity = 1) { return new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness: 0.48, metalness: 0.05, transparent: opacity < 1, opacity }); } function markMaterial(m) { if (!m) return; m.userData.baseOpacity = m.opacity ?? 1; m.userData.baseTransparent = !!m.transparent; } function rememberMats(obj) { obj.traverse(o => { if (Array.isArray(o.material)) o.material.forEach(markMaterial); else markMaterial(o.material); }); } function setGroupDim(g, active) { const factor = active ? 1 : 0.28; g.traverse(o => { const mats = Array.isArray(o.material) ? o.material : (o.material ? [o.material] : []); for (const m of mats) { if (m.userData.isSelectedAtom) continue; const base = m.userData.baseOpacity ?? 1; m.opacity = Math.max(0.06, base * factor); m.transparent = m.opacity < 0.999 || m.userData.baseTransparent; if ('emissive' in m && !m.userData.isSelectedAtom) m.emissive.setHex(0x000000); m.needsUpdate = true; } }); } function cubeCorners(cx, cy, cz, s) { const h = s / 2, pts = []; for (const x of [-h, h]) for (const y of [-h, h]) for (const z of [-h, h]) pts.push(new THREE.Vector3(cx + x, cy + y, cz + z)); return pts; } function faceCenters(cx, cy, cz, s) { const h = s / 2; return [ new THREE.Vector3(cx + h, cy, cz), new THREE.Vector3(cx - h, cy, cz), new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy + h, cz), new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy - h, cz), new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy, cz + h), new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy, cz - h) ]; } function addCube(group, cx, cy, cz, s, opacity, edgeOpacity = 1) { const box = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(s, s, s), matCube(opacity)); box.position.set(cx, cy, cz); group.add(box); const edges = new THREE.LineSegments( new THREE.EdgesGeometry(new THREE.BoxGeometry(s, s, s)), matLine(0x000000, edgeOpacity) ); edges.position.set(cx, cy, cz); group.add(edges); return { box, edges }; } function addSmallDot(group, p, color, r = 0.035) { const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(r, 18, 12), matSphere(color)); m.position.copy(p); group.add(m); return m; } function addTopDiagram(type, cx) { const g = new THREE.Group(); const cy = 1.05, cz = 0, s = 0.52; addCube(g, cx, cy, cz, s, 0.46); for (const p of cubeCorners(cx, cy, cz, s)) addSmallDot(g, p, 0x000000, 0.034); if (type === 'bcc') addSmallDot(g, new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy, cz), 0xff1020, 0.035); if (type === 'fcc') for (const p of faceCenters(cx, cy, cz, s)) addSmallDot(g, p, 0xff1020, 0.033); rememberMats(g); scene.add(g); return g; } function contributionText(role) { if (role === 'corner') return '1/8'; if (role === 'face') return '1/2'; return '1'; } function roleName(role) { if (role === 'corner') return 'corner atom'; if (role === 'face') return 'face-centered atom'; return 'body-centered atom'; } function addAtom(group, type, pos, radius, color, role) { const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(radius, 40, 24), matSphere(color)); mesh.position.copy(pos); mesh.userData.atomInfo = { type, role, contribution: contributionText(role), baseScale: 1 }; group.add(mesh); atoms.push(mesh); registerInteractive(mesh, { title: `${TYPES[type].name}: ${roleName(role)}`, tooltip: `Click: ${roleName(role)} contributes ${contributionText(role)}`, body: `A ${roleName(role)} is shared by neighboring unit cells. Its fractional contribution here is ${contributionText(role)}. Total atoms in a ${TYPES[type].name} unit cell: ${TYPES[type].total}.`, onClick: () => selectAtom(mesh) }); return mesh; } function addBottomModel(type, cx) { const g = new THREE.Group(); const cy = -0.78, cz = 0, s = 0.72; let r; if (type === 'sc') r = s * 0.26; else if (type === 'bcc') r = s * Math.sqrt(3) / 4; else r = s * Math.sqrt(2) / 4; for (const p of cubeCorners(cx, cy, cz, s)) addAtom(g, type, p, r, 0x9a9ca1, 'corner'); if (type === 'bcc') addAtom(g, type, new THREE.Vector3(cx, cy, cz), r, 0xe66a25, 'body'); if (type === 'fcc') for (const p of faceCenters(cx, cy, cz, s)) addAtom(g, type, p, r, 0xe66a25, 'face'); addCube(g, cx, cy, cz, s, 0.22); rememberMats(g); scene.add(g); return g; } function makeFrame(cx, cy, w, h) { const pts = [ new THREE.Vector3(cx - w / 2, cy - h / 2, -0.62), new THREE.Vector3(cx + w / 2, cy - h / 2, -0.62), new THREE.Vector3(cx + w / 2, cy + h / 2, -0.62), new THREE.Vector3(cx - w / 2, cy + h / 2, -0.62) ]; const loop = new THREE.LineLoop(new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(pts), new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0xf2c200, linewidth: 2 })); scene.add(loop); selectedFrames.push(loop); return loop; } for (const type of typeOrder) { const x = cols[type]; groupsByType[type] = [addTopDiagram(type, x), addBottomModel(type, x)]; } const topFrame = makeFrame(cols.sc, 1.05, 0.88, 0.82); const bottomFrame = makeFrame(cols.sc, -0.78, 1.12, 1.2); setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }, heightFraction: 0.82, target: [0, 0.02, 0], distanceScale: 1.5 }); addLabel('Lattice point locations', new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.72, 0), { fontSize: '24px', bold: true, offset: [0, -8] }); addLabel('Cubic unit cells', new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.17, 0), { fontSize: '24px', bold: true }); const captionLabels = { sc: addLabel('Simple cubic', new THREE.Vector3(cols.sc, -1.72, 0), { fontSize: '24px', bold: true, offset: [0, 6] }), bcc: addLabel('Body-centered cubic', new THREE.Vector3(cols.bcc, -1.72, 0), { fontSize: '24px', bold: true, offset: [0, 6] }), fcc: addLabel('Face-centered cubic', new THREE.Vector3(cols.fcc, -1.72, 0), { fontSize: '24px', bold: true, offset: [0, 6] }) }; let currentType = 'sc'; let selectedAtom = null; const statusEl = document.getElementById('cellStatus'); const buttons = { sc: document.getElementById('btnSC'), bcc: document.getElementById('btnBCC'), fcc: document.getElementById('btnFCC') }; function resetAtomHighlight() { if (!selectedAtom) return; const m = selectedAtom.material; m.userData.isSelectedAtom = false; if ('emissive' in m) m.emissive.setHex(0x000000); selectedAtom.scale.setScalar(selectedAtom.userData.atomInfo.baseScale || 1); selectedAtom = null; } function setStatusForType(type) { statusEl.innerHTML = `Selected: ${TYPES[type].name}
Total atoms per unit cell: ${TYPES[type].total}`; } function selectType(type) { currentType = type; resetAtomHighlight(); for (const t of typeOrder) { const active = t === type; for (const g of groupsByType[t]) setGroupDim(g, active); if (buttons[t]) buttons[t].classList.toggle('active', active); if (captionLabels[t]) captionLabels[t].div.style.opacity = active ? '1' : '0.38'; } topFrame.position.x = cols[type] - cols.sc; bottomFrame.position.x = cols[type] - cols.sc; setStatusForType(type); } function selectAtom(atom) { const info = atom.userData.atomInfo; selectType(info.type); selectedAtom = atom; const m = atom.material; m.userData.isSelectedAtom = true; if ('emissive' in m) m.emissive.setHex(0xffd21a); atom.scale.setScalar(1.15); statusEl.innerHTML = `Selected: ${TYPES[info.type].name}
` + `Clicked: ${roleName(info.role)}
` + `Fractional contribution: ${info.contribution}
` + `Total atoms per unit cell: ${TYPES[info.type].total}`; } buttons.sc.addEventListener('click', () => selectType('sc')); buttons.bcc.addEventListener('click', () => selectType('bcc')); buttons.fcc.addEventListener('click', () => selectType('fcc')); selectType('sc'); // @FIGURE_CODE_END
